assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the incretin effect and proglucagon processing to receptor-agonist drugs, transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and is now reshaping cardiometabolic medicine. It is a clear chain from physiological discovery to a therapy with very large patient impact, and a prize would recognize both mechanism and translation.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 biology and its physiological and therapeutic actions; Knudsen led development of the long-acting analogues liraglutide and semaglutide. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is credited in the supplied list and its weight is contested, so a three-person configuration leaves her out and that choice is a real fairness question.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of mechanistic work and large outcome trials across diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular endpoints independently confirm benefit. Timing is favourable given the clinical scale.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener (not on the credited list), Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is disputed in the literature and I have not verified the details.
Whether a physiology-plus-drug-development split is the right framing for the prize.
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed to tumour antigens produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. The concept, receptor design and clinical proof are original and clearly impactful.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design and costimulation concepts, June led the pivotal clinical translation, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Other early CAR originators (e.g. Eshhar) are not on the supplied list, so the three-person set is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across multiple approved products and independent trials in haematological cancers; limited success in solid tumours and notable toxicities mean the story is mature for liquid tumours but still evolving overall.
uncertainties: Omission of other foundational contributors and the weight to give adoptive cell therapy versus CAR design.
Recent signals on secondary T-cell malignancies; my recollection should not be treated as verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is among the most widely used tools in the field, from circuit mapping to behaviour and early therapeutic efforts. The discovery of channelrhodopsins and their adaptation to neurons is original and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin function; Deisseroth, Boyden and others demonstrated neuronal use, with Bamberg and Miesenböck also credited. Six credited names cannot fit into a prize, and the choice of the demonstration side between Deisseroth, Boyden and Miesenböck is a serious allocation difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature as a technique with exhaustive independent confirmation; therapeutic translation is only beginning, so the case rests on tool impact.
uncertainties: Whom to credit for the neuronal demonstration and the chance of an intractable dispute.
This is a method award, which the committee weighs against disease-relevant discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeting the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one, and established the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. Clarity and patient impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound programme, Druker drove the clinical proof of concept, and Sawyers contributed key work on resistance and second-generation inhibitors. Brian Druker, Lydon and Sawyers are a plausible trio, but the upstream Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoveries were made by others, not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature with decades of survival data and independent confirmation across kinase-inhibitor classes.
uncertainties: Prior recognition elsewhere does not bear on merit; the question is whether the targeted-therapy paradigm is better recognized now than later.
The contribution of Rowley and the BCR-ABL discoverers lies outside this credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling pathway from the ER to the nucleus, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and downstream relevance for secretory biology, metabolic disease, neurodegeneration and cancer. It is conceptually elegant and clearly original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central figures, with convergent identification of the IRE1-HAC1 pathway and later mammalian elaboration. The two-person configuration is clean and credit appears reasonably settled.
assessment.maturity: Mature: strong independent confirmation across yeast and mammals, with a large follow-on literature; therapeutic translation is still modest.
uncertainties: Other contributors to the broader ER stress response (e.g. Ron, Harding, Kaufman, Walter's collaborators) may be argued for; I have not verified the extent of their independent claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a lethal infant disease into a treatable one and validating splice-switching oligonucleotides as a platform.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the target sequence, and Bennett led the oligonucleotide chemistry and development at Ionis. The two-person configuration is coherent, though others in SMA genetics (Melki, Lefebvre) established the disease gene and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with strong randomized trial evidence and years of clinical follow-up, though recognition may be somewhat early relative to field consolidation.
uncertainties: Weight of the underlying SMN gene discovery versus therapy development.
Competition with other RNA therapeutic achievements and with the siRNA field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR was identified as the target of rapamycin and defined a central nutrient and growth-signalling hub with implications for metabolism, ageing, immunosuppression and cancer. The discovery is original and its conceptual influence is very broad.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and recognized its role in growth control; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin chemical biology contributed to target identification. Sabatini's contribution to mTORC1 nutrient sensing is credited in the list, but I leave him out here as the attribution is less settled and I cannot verify the issues that might bear on it.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with large independent literature and clinical use of rapalogs; clinical efficacy of mTOR inhibitors is narrower than the biological reach.
uncertainties: Attribution among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and the earlier rapamycin discoverers.
Gap between biological importance and clinical benefit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING identified how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune and interferon responses, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence. It is a clear, novel mechanism with broad consequences.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are also credited and their contributions are real but more incremental in my reading, so a two-person set is plausible though not undisputed.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature mechanistically with substantial independent confirmation, but therapeutic exploitation is still in trials, which makes timing somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the credit between Chen and Barber and the work of others is fairly balanced.
